correctness.rationale: With the observed-vertex transition kernel, direct stationary balance gives pi_c=1/(2-p) for hub resetting and pi_c=(1-p)/(2-p) for leaf resetting. Row-entropies give (H+(1-p)log m)/(2-p) and (H+(1-p)F_m)/(2-p), where F_m is entropy of (p+(1-p)/m,(1-p)/m,...). F_m<log m gives strict hub advantage. The hub derivative is log[(1-p)/(m p^2)]/(2-p)^2, uniquely zero at 1-p=m p^2. At leaf, the exact collision loss G_m, positive trial gain at p=m^-3/4, global localization m^-4/5<p_opt<m^-7/10, and uniform derivative log(1/p)-(3/4)log m+o(1) prove every optimum p~m^-3/4 and gain~m^-3/4; the hub gain~m^-1/2/2. Independent full-state stationary matrix calculations checked both roots for m=2,4,11 and three p values each (18 values); this corroborates, not proves, the limits.

originality.rationale: The classical Perron maximal-entropy walk theorem accounts for the hub optimized benchmark, and Wang–Chen provide the general resetting entropy framework and investigate root dependence on Cayley trees. Neither the accessible scientific statements nor the published Resultary regular-graph and complete-graph findings imply the globally optimized leaf-star p~m^-3/4 law. This is a qualified best-of-knowledge PASS for the leaf contribution, not a claim that the hub benchmark is new.
residual_risks: Complete original Wang–Chen 2022 PDF was not accessible in this run, so a buried equivalent leaf asymptotic cannot be ruled out.
The hub optimized rate itself is a known Perron benchmark; only the sharp leaf contrast warrants originality.
No finite-m uniqueness for leaf optimum; excludes hidden reset labels, nonuniform walks and other graphs.
